meaning:
πλεονάζω
(πλέον), [in LXX for עֲדַף, רָבָה, etc. ;]
I. Intrans.
1. Of persons;
(a) to abound in (Arist.);
(b) to superabound: 2Co.8:15 (LXX).
2. Of things, to abound, superabound: Rom.5:20 6:1, 2Co.4:15, Php.4:17, 2Th.1:3, 2Pe.1:8.
II. Trans. (Num.26:54, Psa.71:21; not cl, see Lft., Notes, 48 f.), to make to abound: 1Th.3:12 (cf. ὑπερ-πλεονάζω).†
SYN.: περισσεύω, q.v (AS)

elsewhere.note: The law came in that the trespass might abound; but where sin abounded, grace abounded more exceedingly;
For all things are for your sakes, that the grace, being multiplied through the many, may cause the thanksgiving to abound to the glory of God.
Not that I seek for the gift, but I seek for the fruit that increases to your account.
May the Lord make you to increase and abound in love toward one another, and toward all men, even as we also do toward you,
We are bound to always give thanks to God for you, brothers, even as it is appropriate, because your faith grows exceedingly, and the love of each and every…
For if these things are yours and abound, they make you to not be idle or unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
